# Extension Capabilities Reference

This chapter is a quick, self-contained reference for Colophon's
distinctive patterns — the handful of things plain Markdown can't
express on its own, shown together in one place so you can see the
actual syntax without reading a full chapter of prose around it. For
the narrative walkthrough, see Chapters 1 and 2. For the complete
written documentation, see the main README and
`docs/BOOK-CREATION-GUIDE.md`.

## A captioned table

Markdown pipe tables always put their caption above the table, with
no way to move it. For a caption below the table — and a real entry
in the List of Tables — write the table in raw LaTeX instead:

```{=latex}
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.3\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.6\linewidth}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\rowcolor{giTableHeaderShade}
\textbf{Term} & \textbf{Definition} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}Extension & Reusable Quarto packaging for a project type, format, or filter. \\
\bottomrule
\caption{\label{tbl-example-terms}A minimal captioned table, built from the ``Captioned Table'' snippet.}
\end{longtable}
```

## A captioned figure

Figures are simpler — plain Markdown, no raw LaTeX needed. The
caption prints below the image by default, and a `fig-alt` attribute
gives you a separate description for accessibility:

![A placeholder image, standing in for a real figure.](logo-placeholder.png){#fig-example width="40%" fig-alt="A placeholder box with the toolkit's default logo text."}

## A landscape table

A wide table gets its own rotated page — everything before and after
it stays portrait:

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
\giLandscapeHeader

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\rowcolor{giTableHeaderShade}
\textbf{Column A} & \textbf{Column B} & \textbf{Column C} & \textbf{Column D} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}Row 1 & Data & Data & Data \\
\bottomrule
\caption{\label{tbl-example-landscape}A wide table that needed the extra room.}
\end{longtable}

\giLandscapeFooter
\end{landscape}
```

## Patterns shown elsewhere, not here

Two more patterns replace a chapter heading entirely, or mark a
transition point in the whole book, rather than fitting inside an
ordinary chapter like this one — so rather than show them as inert
text, this toolkit actually uses them for real, right after this
chapter: Chapter 4 is a genuine landscape-only chapter (see
`landscape-chapter-example.qmd`), and Appendix A right after it
demonstrates the real switch from numbered chapters to lettered
appendices (see `appendix-example.qmd`).
